headline: Approved $4.99 monthly virtual voicemail service for the Museum through NumberBarn.
summary: The Museum will use a virtual voicemail service through NumberBarn at $4.99 per month. The motion passed by voice vote with no opposition. The meeting also covered a McKinney dairy farm history project, Derryfest planning, junior historian recruiting, and off-site storage.
decisions: Approved a museum virtual voicemail service through NumberBarn at $4.99 per month by voice vote with no opposition.

decision_evidence.quote: Jerry moved to establish a museum virtual voicemail service through NumberBarn at $4.99 per month. Lynne seconded the motion. Following a voice vote, the Chair announced no opposition and declared the motion passed.

decision_titles: Virtual voicemail service for the Museum
plain_text:
The Derry Heritage Commission Meeting Minutes
Monday, August 3, 2026
7:00 PM — 3rd Floor Training Room
Derry Municipal Center
Present: Paul Lindemann, Chairperson, Lynne Mari, Gerald “Jerry” LaCorte
Alternates: Aurora Wetherbee, Janet Wetherbee
Absent: JoelCameron(Alternate), TJ Cullinane(Member)
Guest: Brendena Fleming (ownerof the historicMcKinneydairy farm property,now Pumpkin
Wall Farm, in Derry)
1. Call to Order and Roll Call
The Chaircalled the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. The Pledge ofAllegiance andintroductions followed. -
A quorum wasacknowledged.
2. Guest Presentation — HistoricMcKinney Dairy Farm
Ms. Fleming requested help researchingthe former McKinneydairy farm, particularlyitshistoryfrom
approximately 1920 to 1954. She describedan 1869 farmhouse, formerly ElmcrestFarm, and the care
farm and animal sanctuary now operatingthere.She outlinedcollaborationwith McKinney descendants'on a planned name changerecognizing the historicfarm, a possibleribbon cutting,and a long-term
visionforcontinued nonprofitand communityuse of the property.
Members recommended the Derry PublicLibrary’snewspaperarchives, deed research,and consultation
with localhistorians.The Chairagreed to contact RickHolmes, TJ Cullinane,and Mark Mastromarino andcoordinatefurtherresearch.Members suggested timing a publicannouncement after Derryfest.Ms.Fleming alsoexplainedshe wasreferred to the BuildingDepartment regardingproposed parking
changesand signage. Noproperty, funding or projectapproval was requested or granted.
3. Prior Minutes and Administrative Updates
The Chairreported thatthe June minutes had receivedemail approval from the attendingmembers
except Joel,whose response remained outstanding,and statedthat he would submit them as approved
by a majority.No new motionor vote on the minutes was recordedat thismeeting.
4. Recent Accomplishments
Recent accomplishments includedthree successfulbooths at the Derry Homegrown Farm & Artisan
Market, museum exhibitimprovements and an updated TownHall display.The Chairwill process
outstanding expense reimbursements.
5. Old Business
Boston Post Cane search
The Chair willupdate and circulatethe search announcement, confirm information about the prior
recipient,and determine inquiryprocedures andreplica-cane arrangements.Eligibilitydiscussedwas
age 90 or older,currentDerry residenceand residenceinDerry forthe precedingfive years;the oldest
qualifyingresidentwould be selected.Publicitywould includelocalmedia, socialmedia and Town
Counciloutreach.Janet volunteered to serve as an inquirycoordinator.
Town Hall display
Members supported usingthe upcoming farmers market materialson the settlement of Nutfieldand the
FirstParishMeetinghouse preservationprojectto refreshtheleft displaycabinet.The rightcabinet
would remainin placeforthe time being.
Museum virtual phone and voicemail service — motion approved
The Museum has been without a phoneline forseveralmonths, and the Chair presented possiblevirtual
phone number and voicemailservicesto fillthisgap. Jerrymoved to establisha museum virtual
voicemailservicethrough NumberBarn at $4.99 per month. Lynne seconded the motion. Followinga
voicevote,the Chairannounced no oppositionand declared the motion passed.The Chairwill establish
the service,with voicemailnotificationsand transcriptionrouted by email forvolunteerfollow-up.
6. Museum Events and Staffing
Farmers Market — August 5
The finalbooth of the Museum’s four-market serieswillfeaturethe Nutfieldsettlement and
Meetinghousehistory and preservation.The Chairwillbringmaterialsand arriveat approximately 2:15
p.m. forsetup;market hours are 3-7 p.m. Members will finalizesetup,reliefcoverage ,and opening the
museum at6 p.m.by text,includingabsent TJ inthe coordination.
Summer Chill Out — August 14
The museumplans to participateinthe Town’s event from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the Municipal Center
with Hood-relatedhistorical materials.Organizerswere expected to provide a canopy and table.The
Chairwill transportmaterials,with additionalstaffingto be confirmed. Materialsare to be assembled
during museum hours on August 12.
Derryfest — September 19
Members supported repeatingthe CivilWar themewith reenactors,subjectto confirmationwith Joel.
The event runs 10 a.m.—4 p.m.,with setup earlierand cleanup afterward.Members will advisethe Chair
of availabilityso shiftscan be arranged.The booth mayoffer TJ’sCivilWar book. TJ’savailabilitywas
uncertainbecause of another possiblecommitment.
Regular museum coverage
Members were asked to notifythe Chairof Wednesday absencesuntil a shared onlinecalendaris
available.Recent attendance had improved, particularlyfollowingfarmers market outreach.
7. Junior Historians and Collections
Members discussed rebuildingthe JuniorHistoriansgroup as olderstudents move on. Lynne agreed to
help leadthe effort,with support from other members. School contacts,former participantsand
Derryfestwereidentified as recruitingavenues. Proposed projectsincludedartifactcatalogingand
paintingorinstallingprepared slatsat Lucy Gregg’scemeteryplot, with a possibleSeptember work
party.Members willdevelop defined projectsand match tasksto studentinterests.
The Chairproposed winter trainingto enter the backlogof severalhundred inventorysheets intothe
Omeka online collectionsdatabase. Improved recordswould support research,exhibitpreparation,and
locatingartifacts.Members and juniorhistorianscould perform data entry remotely aftertraining.
White cabinets, books and deaccessioning
The white-cabinetinventorywas reported complete and grouped by subject.Members will schedule a
separate work sessionto reorganizethe contents.Lynne and Janet plannedto begin reviewingboxed
booksthe followingday. Books must be checked againstthe 2011 inventoryand RickHolmes’s
requested review respected before disposal.The Chairwillrevisitthe libraryagreement and clarifyTown
requirements,includingwhether appropriatereferencematerialscan be transferredto the library.No
specificdisposalor transferwas approved.
Sales display and internet access
Members supported repurposingthe displaycase near the Pinkertonareafor books, shirts,cards and
otheravailable merchandise, afterfindingsuitablehomesfor its currentcontents.The goal ismore to
share these items with the publicthan to maximize income, and pricing,inventoryand payment
arrangements remain tc be developed. The Chairwillfollowup with Town ITDepartment on museum
Wi-Fi to supportresearch, collectionsaccess, potential sales and future exhibit QR codes.
Off-site storage
The Chairwill coordinate moving plasticbinsfrom the smallerrented unitintothe largerunitcontaining
the sleighand buggy.This willprovide accesstofiling cabinetsbelievedto contain historicalresearch
records.Historiansand members can then review the papers and determine preservationneeds. The
moveis to be scheduled; no disposalwas authorized.
8.- Outreach, Research and Programs
Aurora agreed tolead increasedsocialmedia activity,includingshort historyvideos and possibleartifact
features.Members emphasized accurate identificationand research,regularpostingand use ofexisting
channels.Paid promotion wasdiscussed asa possibility;no advertisingbudget was approved.
Members supported producing museum business/contactcards once the new phone number is
available,with Aurora having professionalexperienceassisting with printing.Existingrackcardswill
remain inuse.
Members were encouraged to propose researchedarticles forthe museum website andcirculate drafts
for review.Aurora expressedinterest inthe Indigenousguide knownas Old Ezekieland the historyof
the property and marchland near which helived.
Recent cemetery tours led by TJ and Erinwere reported as highlysuccessful,with approximately 50
attendeesat each.A Halloween-themedtour wasanticipated. The Chairreported a December 1
PreservationAllianceprogram atFirst ParishinEastDerry concerning the reuse ofhistoric religious
buildings,includinga Meetinghouse tour.Outdoor Highlandactivitieswere being considered forspring,
likelyMay, with a possibleindoor Founders Weekend eventin April.
Jerryreported continuingcontactwith Parkland regardinghistoricalinformation,images, and possible
artifactsforthe hospitalexhibit.Members discussedassistancewith a displaypanelafter materialsare
received.
9. Adjournment
Lynne made a motion to adjourn and Jerrysecondedit. Afteraskingforany additionalbusiness,the
Chairdeclared the meeting adjourned at 8:57 p.m. The vote was unanimous. The next meeting dateis
Monday, October 5, 2026.
